labeled_by: Claude (Fable 5) from materials-science first principles, BLIND to model output, pre-scoring
note: Sealed labels, written before any Q11 prediction was executed. Expert judgment, not external experimental ground truth; borderline pairs are flagged. Independence caveat: authored by the same assistant that worked on the codebase.

11001.basis: Polysulfide intermediates nucleophilically attack carbonate solvents; Li-S cannot run in carbonate/LiPF6 - this is why Li-S uses ethers

11002.basis: LiTFSI in DOL/DME is the standard Li-S electrolyte salt

11003.basis: Sulfur corrodes copper to Cu2S; sulfur cathodes are cast on Al, never Cu

11004.basis: Al is the standard current collector for sulfur cathodes

11005.basis: Imide salts (TFSI-) fail to passivate Al and cause pitting corrosion above ~3.7 V vs Li - the classic barrier to LiTFSI-only electrolytes

11006.basis: LiPF6 forms a protective AlF3/AlF3-rich passivation layer; the standard commercial pairing

11007.basis: LGPS electrochemical reduction onset is ~1.7 V vs Li; graphite operates near 0.1 V, so LGPS is continuously reduced

11008.basis: Thiophosphate sulfide electrolyte is reduced at graphite's operating potential

11009.basis: Ti(IV) in LATP is reduced to Ti(III) below ~2.4 V vs Li; graphite at 0.1 V reduces it

11010.basis: PEO-LiTFSI is the canonical solid polymer electrolyte system

11011.basis: CMC is a water-soluble binder; aqueous slurry processing is its entire purpose

11012.basis: LTO plateau is ~1.55 V, just below LGPS reduction onset ~1.7 V; LGPS/LTO solid cells are demonstrated but interfacial degradation is reported - BORDERLINE

11014.basis: Acetal (POM) has excellent resistance to ketones and most organic solvents

11015.basis: Acetone crazes and dissolves polycarbonate - a textbook PC failure mode

11016.basis: PTFE is chemically inert to aromatic hydrocarbons

11017.basis: PDMS swells enormously in toluene (swelling ratio ~1.3); standard microfluidics solvent-compatibility knowledge

11018.basis: EPDM has poor resistance to aromatic hydrocarbons and swells badly; EPDM is specified for glycol/brake fluid, not petroleum aromatics

11020.basis: PEEK has excellent hydrolytic stability and is repeatedly steam-sterilizable

11021.basis: PPO/PS is the textbook thermodynamically miscible polymer blend (commercial Noryl)

11022.basis: PC and PS are immiscible with poor interfacial adhesion

11023.basis: Galvanizing: Zn is anodic to steel and sacrificially protects it - a galvanic couple that is deliberately beneficial

11024.basis: Large galvanic potential difference drives Al corrosion, plus brittle Al-Fe intermetallics on joining

11025.basis: Mg is extremely anodic; iron contamination is the classic cause of catastrophic Mg galvanic corrosion

11026.basis: Ti-Fe forms brittle TiFe/TiFe2 intermetallics; direct fusion welding is not viable

11027.basis: Ni-Fe show complete solid solubility (basis of Invar/Ni steels); readily joined

11028.basis: Ag-Sn forms Ag3Sn, the intended strengthening phase in SAC solders

11029.basis: Kovar CTE ~5.5 ppm/K vs fused silica ~0.55 ppm/K; Kovar is matched to borosilicate, not silica - seal cracks

11030.basis: Both austenitic Ni-Fe-Cr alloys with similar CTE; routinely welded in practice

11031.basis: Mullite and SiC have close CTE and are co-used in mullite-SiC refractory composites

11032.basis: Zirconia destabilizes hydroxyapatite during co-sintering (HA decomposes to TCP/CaO and zirconia is destabilized) - a well-known bioceramic incompatibility

11033.basis: Hexagonal BN is chemically compatible with silicon nitride and used as a release/interface phase

11034.basis: SiO2/TiO2 is the standard low-index/high-index dielectric multilayer pair

11035.basis: MgO and TiO2 react at sintering temperature to form magnesium titanates (MgTiO3/Mg2TiO4) rather than coexisting

11036.basis: Cu diffuses rapidly into Bi2Te3 and poisons the thermoelectric contact; a Ni diffusion barrier is required

11037.basis: Ni is the standard diffusion-barrier/contact metallization for Bi2Te3 thermoelectric legs

11038.basis: Diamond-on-Si lattice mismatch is ~52%; heteroepitaxy is not viable without exotic intermediate layers

11039.basis: Graded SiGe buffers to pure Ge are the standard route to Ge-on-Si virtual substrates

11040.basis: InN on Si has very large lattice and thermal expansion mismatch; no coherent epitaxy
